items.name: Samsung Solve for Tomorrow
items.cost: Free · up to $50,000 for your school
items.note: Teams of public-school students in grades 6–12 use STEM to solve a community problem. A teacher submits the first-round answers. No citizenship rule is listed. Semifinalists make a project video (Jan 20 – Mar 3), and finalists pitch live in spring. The prizes go to the school, not to you.
items.act: Next step: if a teacher can submit tonight, do it. If not, plan for the cycle that opens around Sept 30, 2027.

items.name: Berkeley Math Tournament (BMT) 2026 Online
items.dlabel: Nov 27, 2026 (11:59 PM PT); Power Round Nov 28–29, live contest Dec 5, 2026
items.note: Online version of one of the major college-run high school math tournaments, with individual, team and Power rounds. Open to students in grade 12 or below anywhere, including international students; no coach needed, and students can register solo or form teams of up to 6.
items.act: Register on ContestDojo by Nov 27, 11:59 PM PT, get a parent to sign the UC Berkeley waiver in the portal, and use the Teammate Finder sheet to fill out a team of at least 4.

items.name: Lumiere Scholars Essay Award
items.dlabel: Register by Nov 30, 2026 (11:59 PM ET); essay due Dec 20, 2026 (11:59 PM ET)
items.note: Free academic essay contest of up to 2,000 words, open to high school students from any country. Gold wins $1,000 cash, Silver $500 and Bronze $300 (each plus a Lumiere program scholarship); other awards are tuition credits for Lumiere programs only. An academic referee's email is required.
items.act: Register free by Nov 30, 2026 and get a teacher's email as referee; the essay is due Dec 20.

items.name: USA Mathematical Talent Search (USAMTS) Year 38
items.dlabel: Nov 30, 2026 (Round 2, 10 PM ET); Round 3 due early 2027 (date not yet posted)
items.note: Free, proof-based contest with written solutions and about a month per round. Students may join at Round 2 or 3 without having done Round 1, and prizes are awarded at year end. The rules say participants must be 'US citizens or residents' who haven't finished high school, so a student living in the U.S. should qualify.
items.act: Register at usamts.org/register and submit Round 2 solutions online by Nov 30, 10 PM ET, or at least join for Round 3 in the new year.

items.name: Harvard Undergraduate Capital Partners High School Investment Pitch Competition
items.note: A pitch competition run by Harvard undergraduates: Round 1 (pitch deck or memo) is due Dec 23, 2026, Round 2 (video) Jan 18, 2027, and virtual finals are in February, with $3,000 in prizes. Open to grades 8-12; the page states no citizenship rule.
items.act: Decide by Nov 30, 2026 whether to register a team (registration closes in 3 days); email contact@harvardcap.org to confirm an H-4 student can compete.
items.question: I'm a high school junior at a U.S. public school on an H-4 dependent visa (not a citizen or green card holder); am I eligible to compete in the High School Investment Pitch Competition?

items.name: BigFuture Scholarships (Class of 2028)
items.note: Students in the class of 2028 at any U.S. high school earn drawing entries by completing six College Board planning steps, such as a career list or college list. Each month College Board draws $500 awards, and every two months a $40,000 award. There's no citizenship rule, and the FAFSA step allows you to attest that you're legally ineligible.
items.act: Log into BigFuture and save 3 careers and 3 colleges now; entries roll into every later drawing. Do the college-list step before June 30, 2027.

items.name: Naval Science and Engineering Apprenticeship Program (SEAP) 2027
items.org: U.S. Navy / Office of Naval Research (Naval STEM)
items.kind: Paid summer lab internship (about 38 Navy labs)
items.note: An 8-week summer research apprenticeship at Navy labs. It pays a $4,000 stipend for new participants. Applicants must be U.S. citizens, at least 16, and have finished grade 9. Some labs make exceptions for permanent residents, which Krithik is not. It is paid, and H-4 status does not allow paid work without an EAD.
items.act: Skip. The program requires U.S. citizenship and is paid work that H-4 status does not allow.

items.name: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
items.note: The Critical Essay and Journalism categories suit policy writing, and you can enter work you've already written. Open to anyone who attends school and lives in the U.S. Regional results come out Jan 27 and national results Mar 31.
items.act: Next step: use the Region Finder at artandwriting.org/regions with your school's zip code today. Arkansas writing entries are run by the Heartland Writing Region (Crystal Bridges Museum, Bentonville), which is likely your region; check its deadline. The countdown shows the earliest regional deadline (Dec 1).

items.name: Coolidge Scholarship
items.note: A full ride to any U.S. college, chosen in junior year, with an emphasis on public policy. You must be a citizen or permanent resident by Dec 1. The program has no senior-year round.
items.act: Becomes possible only if the green card is issued before Dec 1, 2026.

items.name: U of A Engineering Summer Academy
items.org: University of Arkansas College of Engineering
items.dlabel: Registration opens Dec 1, 2026 (first come, 20 per track)
items.note: A one-week residential engineering camp in Fayetteville (June 20–26, 2027), $700 with scholarships available. The page says students 'entering the 10th through 12th grade during the 2027-2028 academic year are eligible', so a rising senior qualifies. No citizenship rule is stated. Low weight with colleges, but close to home.
items.act: Register on Dec 1 if you want it (first come, 20 per track); email engrcamp@uark.edu if you want to confirm there is no citizenship requirement.
items.question: I'm a junior at Bentonville public schools on an H-4 dependent visa; is there any citizenship or residency requirement to attend the Engineering Summer Academy?

items.name: WIU GenCyber Cybersecurity Camp 2027
items.dlabel: Dec 1, 2026, 11:59 pm CST (student application); recommendation form due Dec 15, 2026
items.cost: Free (travel to Macomb, IL not stated)
items.note: Free 6-day residential cybersecurity camp in Macomb, Illinois (June 6–11, 2027) for 30 incoming 9th–12th graders (15 male, 15 female) with little or no prior cyber experience. The page does not state citizenship or state-residency rules.
items.act: Email PI Tahir Khan (TM-Khan@wiu.edu) to ask about eligibility for an out-of-state H-4 student, complete the one-sitting application by Dec 1, and have a recommender submit the form by Dec 15.
items.question: I'm an incoming 12th grader from Arkansas on an H-4 dependent visa; am I eligible for the WIU GenCyber camp as an out-of-state, non-citizen student?

items.name: FRA Americanism Essay Contest 2026-27
items.diff: Easy–moderate: 350-word essay on the set theme, entered through an FRA sponsor
items.note: Students in grades 7–12 write a 350-word essay through an FRA branch or member. The grand national prize is $1,500, and the top three in each grade get $1,000, $750 and $500. The rules state no citizenship requirement, and entrants must certify that no AI was used. The deadline is only 4 days away and requires finding a sponsor.
items.act: Use the 'find a sponsor' link on the FRA East Coast Region page right away, or skip this year.
items.question: Can an 11th grader in Bentonville, Arkansas who is on an H-4 visa (not a citizen or green card holder) still enter by Dec 1, and which branch or Member-at-Large can sponsor him?

items.name: St. Jude High School Research Immersion
items.org: St. Jude Children's Research Hospital · Memphis
items.note: Research at St. Jude for juniors who are 16 or older, from the Memphis area and nearby Tennessee, Mississippi and Arkansas counties. You must be a citizen or permanent resident, and it pays a stipend, which H-4 status doesn't allow.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives before Dec 4.

items.name: American Rocketry Challenge 2027
items.org: Aerospace Industries Association / National Association of Rocketry
items.note: This is the world's largest student rocketry contest. Teams of 3 to 10 must fly two raw eggs to 800 ft and bring them down within 37 to 40 seconds. The top 100 teams go to the National Finals on May 15, 2027 and share $100,000 in prizes. It is open to students in grades 6 to 12 at a U.S. school or homeschool, and no citizenship rule is stated.
items.act: Find at least two teammates and a school or club sponsor this week, then register the team and pay the $195 fee at apply.rocketrychallenge.org before Dec 6.

items.name: NASA/FAA Dream With Us High School Engineering Challenge
items.diff: Medium · Blue Ribbon judges pick finalists
items.note: A NASA aeronautics design challenge for teams in grades 9 to 12. Finalists give virtual presentations on Apr 2, 2027, and winners are announced Apr 9. It is open to students at any U.S. public, private, parochial or home school, with no citizenship rule stated. AI tools are not allowed.
items.act: Ask a teacher to act as team sponsor and register the team on the NASA challenge page by Dec 8. Have each member create a NASA Gateway account and get a signed parent permission form.

items.name: NASSP Student Service Grants (Standard up to $1,000)
items.diff: Moderate; written project proposal and budget
items.note: Grants of up to $1,000 (Legacy grants up to $3,000 for projects already run) for youth-led service projects. Open to students in the United States aged 13-18 who are current members of NHS, NJHS or a student council with an active NASC membership. No citizenship rule is stated; only students outside the U.S. are excluded.
items.act: Confirm membership in NHS or an NASC-affiliated student council, create an account, get verified by the adviser, and submit the proposal by Dec 8, 2026.

items.name: LEDA Scholars
items.org: Leadership Enterprise for a Diverse America
items.note: A summer at Princeton plus college-application support for public-school juniors with a 3.5+ GPA. You must be a citizen or permanent resident.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives before Dec 9.

items.name: Research Science Institute (RSI)
items.org: Center for Excellence in Education · MIT & Stanford
items.note: Six weeks of mentored research. RSI has two application pools: U.S. citizens and permanent residents apply directly, and international students go through a sponsoring country. An H-4 student at a U.S. school fits neither pool, so ask CEE directly.
items.act: Next step: use the RSI contact form today. You'll need three recommenders, essays and your PSAT/SAT scores (CEE recommends PSAT Math 740+).
items.question: RSI's application has one pool for U.S. citizens and permanent residents and another for international students sponsored by their home country. Since I attend a U.S. school but am neither, which application should I use?

items.name: USA Computing Olympiad (USACO)
items.diff: Gold is hard; Platinum or camp is elite
items.note: Four online contests move you up from Bronze to Platinum, ending with the US Open in March or April. The 2026–27 schedule isn't posted on usaco.org yet (as of Nov 27); last season's first contest was Jan 9–12. Reaching Platinum is a strong signal for computer science.
items.act: Next step: create an account at usaco.org and check its schedule page for the first 2026–27 contest window.

items.name: Kenyon Review Patricia Grodd Poetry Prize
items.cost: Free · full scholarship to a Kenyon Young Writers workshop
items.note: Open only to high school sophomores and juniors: submit one unpublished poem. The winner gets a full scholarship to the Kenyon Review Young Writers workshop, and the winner and runners-up are published in The Kenyon Review. The page doesn't state a citizenship rule; the Kenyon Review lists no email, only a contact form (choose 'Young Writers' or 'Submissions') and phone (740) 427-5208.
items.act: Polish one strong poem and submit it free through Submittable before Dec 15.
items.question: I'm a high school junior at a U.S. public school on an H-4 dependent visa; is there any citizenship or residency requirement for the Patricia Grodd Poetry Prize?

items.name: IEOx Essay Challenge 2026/27
items.diff: Medium · top 40 named, top 5 special awards
items.note: Economics research essay from the International Economics Olympiad. The 2026/27 topic is climate economics (carbon markets, sustainable finance, environmental policy), with 1,500–2,000 words plus an abstract. It is open to high school students worldwide who are under 20 on June 30, 2027.
items.act: Register and submit on ieo-official.org before Dec 15, 2026; read the 2026/27 regulations PDF first.

items.name: MIT Zero Robotics High School Tournament 2027
items.note: Teams of at least 4 high school students write code to control robots in a space-simulation game. The online program runs Jan 11 to Feb 12, 2027, and the final event is Feb 19, 2027. MIT recruits teams from around the world, and the page lists no citizenship rule.
items.act: Recruit three or more teammates, for example from your VEX team, and fill in the registration form linked on the MIT Zero Robotics announcement page by Dec 16.

items.name: Presidential SI (formerly AI) Challenge 2027
items.org: White House / U.S. DOE via ORISE
items.dlabel: Dec 18, 2026, 5 pm ET registration; project due Dec 23, 2026
items.note: National K-12 team AI project challenge (renamed 'Super Intelligence') with state, regional and DC national championships; high school national champions win $10,000-$12,500 each. Every student and the Team Leader must be a US citizen, US national or lawful permanent resident.
items.act: No action; ineligible without a green card. Recheck if the green card is approved before a future cycle.

items.name: NCFL Grand National Tournament
items.dlabel: Dec 20, 2026 (diocesan league registration + dues; late Jan 15/Jan 31 with penalty); tournament May 29–30, 2027
items.cost: $60 school league dues plus entry and travel
items.note: This is a major national tournament in Minneapolis on May 29–30, 2027. Students qualify through an NCFL local league. No Arkansas league was found; a school far from a league can apply for individual membership by Dec 20, or enter as an independent school with one entry for one year. Update Nov 26: NCFL now lists diocesan league registration and dues due Dec 20, 2026 (late until Jan 31 with penalties); individual school membership forms are no longer required.
items.act: Ask the coach to check ncfl.org local leagues for one near Arkansas, or to email the NCFL President about independent entry before Dec 10, 2026.

items.name: YIP Institute Public Policy Fellowship (Winter 2027)
items.note: A youth-run virtual policy fellowship for students ages 13–23. The Winter cohort runs Jan 16–Mar 20, 2027. The page says it is for U.S. students and not international ones, but gives no citizenship rule, and the cost is not stated.
items.act: Email fellowship@yipinstitute.org about the cost and whether U.S.-based H-4 students qualify, then apply by Dec 23, 2026 if it is free.

items.name: SAR Knight Essay Contest (High School)
items.org: National Society Sons of the American Revolution
items.dlabel: Dec 31, 2026 (most state societies; Arkansas date — confirm)
items.diff: Medium · chapter, then state, then national
items.note: An 800–1,200 word essay on an event, person or ideal connected to the American Revolution, the Declaration of Independence or the Constitution, for grades 9–12. State winners go to national judging by Mar 15. The rules say 'US Citizen and Legal Resident students', so H-4 eligibility is unclear.
items.act: When contacting the Arkansas SAR education chair about the oration contest, also ask for the essay deadline and whether H-4 students are eligible.

items.name: American Computer Science League (ACSL) 2026-27
items.dlabel: Dec 31, 2026 (advisor registers team); Contest 1 must start by Jan 10, 2027
items.note: School-based CS contest with four online rounds (through May 23, 2027) and invitational Finals on May 29, 2027. A teacher advisor must register the team; students cannot register themselves. The site does not state a citizenship rule.
items.act: Ask a CS or math teacher to register a Senior-division team at acsl.org before Dec 31, 2026.

items.name: Gen and Kelly Tanabe Scholarship
items.note: A $1,000 scholarship for students in grades 9-12, college or graduate school, judged mainly on a personal statement. There are two rounds a year (July 31 and December 31). Applicants must be a 'legal resident of the U.S.' and the page doesn't say whether visa holders qualify.
items.act: Ask through the contact page whether H-4 holders qualify, then submit the personal statement by Dec 31.
items.question: Does a high school junior living in the U.S. on an H-4 dependent visa count as a 'legal resident of the U.S.' for the Gen and Kelly Tanabe Scholarship?

items.name: Courage to Grow Scholarship
items.note: A $1,000 scholarship for high school juniors, seniors and college students with a GPA of 2.5 or higher, based on a 250-word essay. It is limited to U.S. citizens only.
items.act: Not eligible: U.S. citizens only.

items.name: MIT THINK Scholars
items.note: You submit a proposal of up to 10 pages for a STEM project you haven't built yet. Finalists get weekly MIT mentorship and a trip to MIT. You need a permanent U.S. address, but not citizenship. It's a good fit if you have an engineering idea but no lab.
items.act: Next step: pick an idea you can complete in one semester for $1,000, and spend December on the background research.

items.name: Rockefeller University Summer Science Research Program
items.note: Seven weeks of full-time biomedical lab research (9 to 5 on weekdays) for juniors and seniors who are 16 by June 21, 2027. The program lists no citizenship rule. Students from outside the New York area may apply, but Rockefeller won't help with housing or travel.
items.act: Next step: confirm you'd have a place to stay in New York, then line up recommendations. They're due with your application on Jan 4.

items.name: MIT Battlecode 2027 (High School Tournament)
items.dlabel: Kickoff Jan 4, 2027 (registration opens Dec 1; finals Jan 31; confirm)
items.note: Month-long AI programming game competition run by MIT, with a separate High School Tournament for teams made up only of high schoolers. The prize pool is over $40,000. The site says 'anyone is welcome to participate' and student teams, including non-MIT ones, can win prizes.
items.act: Register a team at play.battlecode.org after Dec 1, 2026 and mark High School eligibility on the team profile before the kickoff on Jan 4.

items.name: Non-Trivial Research Fellowship 2027
items.dlabel: Jan 4, 2027 final (priority Dec 15, 2026; years inferred, confirm)
items.note: Free online research incubator on pressing global problems: a 5-week Foundations course, a 9-week summer Fellowship (June 7-Aug 13, 2027) with $1,000 project grants for about 200 Fellows, and up to 20 $10,000 scholarships. Ages 14-20 in June 2027, not yet at university, applicants anywhere in the world.
items.act: Complete the free online application (about 1 hour: profile, brainteasers, logic puzzles) by the Dec 15 priority deadline.

items.name: IASC Asteroid Search Campaign
items.org: International Astronomical Search Collaboration (NASA citizen science)
items.dlabel: Register before Jan 4, 2027 campaign start (confirm; later campaigns run too)
items.note: Teams of 2 or more analyze telescope images to find asteroids; confirmed finds are credited to the team. Participants come from 100+ countries. Listed 2027 campaigns run Jan 4-28, 2027.
items.act: Form a team of 2 or more, download the registration form and email it to IASC.

items.name: Taco Bell Live Más Scholarship
items.note: A passion-based scholarship judged on a short video about your goals, not on grades or test scores. Open to ages 16–26 who are on track to finish high school. Applicants must be a 'legal resident of the 50 United States', which may or may not include H-4 status.
items.act: Email the Taco Bell Foundation to ask whether a dependent visa holder counts as a legal resident, then script a 2-minute video.
items.question: I'm a 16-year-old high school student living in Arkansas on an H-4 dependent visa; do I count as a 'legal resident of the 50 United States' for the Live Más Scholarship?

items.name: Harvard International Economics Essay Competition (HIEEC)
items.note: Economics essay contest run by Harvard's undergraduate economics association. It is open to high school students anywhere in the world, and juniors compete in the Grades 11–12 division. Winners are published on the website and every award recipient gets a certificate.
items.act: Choose a 2026–27 prompt on thehuea.org and submit the essay and the $25 fee before Jan 5, 2027.

items.name: Yale Young Global Scholars
items.note: Two weeks at Yale with a social science track (politics, law, economics) and a STEM track. Open to students from every country, with aid on the same terms for everyone.
items.act: Next step: request financial aid inside the application by Jan 6. You can't request it after decisions come out.

items.name: Stanford University Mathematics Camp (SUMaC)
items.note: An intensive proof-based math program at Stanford (residential) or online, open to students in grades 10 and 11. The admissions page doesn't state a citizenship rule. Financial aid is due about a week after the application.
items.act: Ask SUMaC whether non-citizens at U.S. schools can apply, then start the admission problems over winter break.
items.question: Can students on an H-4 visa who attend a U.S. high school apply to SUMaC, and are they considered domestic or international applicants for admission and financial aid?

items.name: NRA Youth Education Summit (Y.E.S.)
items.cost: Free (all expenses paid) · up to $40,000 in scholarships
items.note: A six-day leadership and government program in Washington, D.C. (July 27 – Aug 1, 2027) for rising juniors and seniors, with competition for college scholarships. Requires a three-page Second Amendment essay, personal statement, transcript, three recommendations and an interview. No citizenship rule is stated on the announcement.
items.act: Decide whether the Second Amendment essay topic fits you; if so, ask the NRA Foundation whether non-citizens are eligible.

items.name: AAJA JCamp 2027
items.cost: Free, including domestic airfare, campus housing and meals
items.note: A free, selective 6-day journalism training camp held alongside AAJA's national convention, open to high school sophomores and juniors (no need to be Asian or an AAJA member). International students may apply if they are physically in the U.S. before and after camp.
items.act: Submit the JCamp application on AAJA's Submittable portal by Jan 10, 2027.

items.name: JFK Profile in Courage Essay Contest
items.note: 700–1,000 words analyzing an act of political courage by a U.S. elected official who served in or after 1917. Open to U.S. high school students in grades 9–12. Prizes: $10,000 first, $3,000 second, $1,000 for each finalist.
items.act: Next step: ask an English or history teacher to be your nominating teacher. Choose a lesser-known official, because well-known subjects score lower. You need at least five sources, and essays where AI use is detected are disqualified.

items.name: IAC Northwest Arkansas Regional: Political Science / US History National Qualifying Exams
items.org: International Academic Competitions (Science, History & Geography Bees)
items.kind: Academic competition (qualifying exam leading to nationals)
items.dlabel: Jan 11, 2027 (registration; event Jan 23, 2027 at UA Fort Smith)
items.cost: $20 per exam (online or in person); nationals travel extra
items.note: This season, high schoolers at the Jan 23, 2027 NWA regional (UA Fort Smith) take Varsity National Qualifying Exams instead of buzzer bees. A score of 75 or above, or a top-half finish in the division, qualifies for nationals, such as the National Political Science Bee in Arlington, VA on Apr 22, 2027. The exams can also be taken online until Apr 16, 2027. The page does not mention citizenship.
items.act: Register for the Political Science (and possibly US History) exam by Jan 11, 2027, or take it online before Apr 16.
items.question: Is there any citizenship or residency requirement to qualify for and compete at the 2027 National Political Science Bee, for a U.S. high school student on an H-4 visa?

items.name: Bezos Scholars Program
items.note: A year-long leadership program for juniors that includes the Aspen Ideas Festival (June 24–30, 2027) and a community project. The program lists no citizenship rule. You must attend a U.S. public school that is Title I, has at least 30% of students on free or reduced lunch, or is rated high-need by the state. Schools that produced a Scholar in 2025 or 2026 can't apply.
items.act: Next step: ask your counselor whether your school qualifies. If it does, choose an educator mentor, who has to apply with you.
items.question: If my school meets the Title I or high-need requirement, am I eligible to apply as a student who is not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident?

items.name: AMA UAS4STEM Drone Competition 2027
items.note: A drone mission competition for middle and high school teams. Prize money goes up to $2,500 plus Skydio drones in the Advanced level. The page gives no grade or citizenship rules.
items.act: Email AMAUAS4STEM@modelaircraft.org to confirm eligibility and the fee before registering by Jan 12.

items.name: Arkansas TSA State Conference (path to National TSA/TEAMS)
items.dlabel: Jan 13, 2027, 5:00 PM (registration closes); portfolios and pre-event submissions Jan 20, 2027, 11:59 PM
items.note: The state conference is March 2–3, 2027 in Hot Springs. It has events such as Engineering Design, Robotics, Drone Challenge, Coding, Software Development and Debating Technological Issues, and top finishers go on to the National TSA/TEAMS conference on June 23–27, 2027 in Orlando. You must enter through a school TSA chapter. The page gives no citizenship rule.
items.act: Ask your school's CTE or engineering teacher whether Bentonville has a TSA chapter. If it does, get added to the chapter roster before registration opens Dec 1.
items.question: I'm a junior at a Bentonville public school on an H-4 dependent visa; is there any citizenship requirement to compete at the Arkansas TSA State Conference and advance to nationals?

items.name: Aspirnaut Lu-Springer High School Summer Research Internship
items.cost: Free; housing on Vanderbilt campus; $2,000 salary
items.note: Six-week biomedical lab research internship at VUMC in Nashville, with recruiting aimed at rural students. Applicants must be 15 or older, and international students may apply (no visa sponsorship). It pays a $2,000 salary, which is paid work H-4 status doesn't allow, so ask whether you can join unpaid.
items.act: Email Aspirnaut to ask whether an H-4 student can take part without the salary; if yes, get transcripts and recommendation letters in by Jan 13.

items.name: Diamond Challenge
items.note: Teams pitch a business or social-innovation idea. The competition is international, so citizenship isn't a factor. It's a good fit if you want to turn an engineering or policy idea into a venture.
items.act: Next step: form a team of 2–4 students and draft the concept submission.

items.name: F=ma Physics Exam
items.note: The first round of the U.S. Physics Olympiad. It's open to anyone attending a U.S. school, so you can take it. The next round (USAPhO, March 14) requires citizenship or a green card, so the realistic goal is a strong F=ma score.
items.act: Ask your physics teacher to register your school before Jan 14.

items.name: UTHealth McGovern High School Summer Research Program
items.org: UTHealth Houston · McGovern Medical School (Biochemistry & Molecular Biology)
items.note: Four weeks of lab placement in Houston (June 7 – July 2, 2027) with weekly clinician talks and a final symposium; juniors and seniors who are 16 by June 7 are the target. The page lists no citizenship rule. It costs $4,000 and doesn't provide housing, so it carries less weight than free, selective programs.
items.act: Only if you could stay in Houston and the fee is manageable: ask the program whether non-citizens are eligible, then send a transcript, two references and a personal statement by Jan 15, 2027.

items.name: National High School Ethics Bowl – Arkansas Regional
items.org: National High School Ethics Bowl (UNC Parr Center) / UA Little Rock
items.diff: Medium · team of 3–7; regional winners advance to nationals
items.note: Teams of 3–7 students talk through ethical cases on policy and society in a civil, debate-like format. The Arkansas regional is Feb 6, 2027 at UA Little Rock, and the winners can advance to the national championship. Students must be in grades 9–12 at an accredited U.S. high school with a school-approved coach; the site says nothing about citizenship.
items.act: Ask the debate coach to sponsor a team, then email the UA Little Rock organizers (jxmcauliffe@ualr.edu) and register with NHSEB HQ by Jan 15, 2027.
items.question: I'm a junior at a Bentonville public high school on an H-4 dependent visa; is there any citizenship requirement to compete in the Arkansas High School Ethics Bowl and at nationals?

items.name: Summer Academic Research Experience (SARE) at Johns Hopkins
items.org: Johns Hopkins School of Medicine, Cell Biology
items.cost: Free; $3,000 stipend on completion; no housing
items.note: Eight-week lab research program in Baltimore for rising 10th-12th graders. Household income must be at or below 200% of the federal poverty level, plus one more criterion such as first-generation college-bound. The page states no citizenship rule; the stipend may conflict with H-4 rules and the family must arrange housing.
items.act: Check whether the family meets the income and first-gen criteria; if so, apply by Jan 15, 2027 and ask about stipend rules for H-4 students.

items.name: USC Bovard Scholars
items.cost: Free; USC pays travel for students from outside Southern California
items.note: A free 3-week residential leadership and college-access program at USC, followed by a year of admissions coaching, for juniors 'actively enrolled in a high school curriculum within the U.S.' with financial need, a 4.0+ weighted GPA and Algebra II or higher. The page doesn't state a citizenship rule.
items.act: Check whether the family meets the financial-need requirement, email the program to confirm H-4 eligibility, then apply by Jan 15.
items.question: I'm a junior at a U.S. public high school on an H-4 dependent visa (not a citizen or permanent resident); am I eligible to apply to USC Bovard Scholars?

items.name: Air Force Academy Summer Seminar 2027
items.note: A one-week 'live like a cadet' seminar for juniors. Applicants must be U.S. citizens.
items.act: Not eligible (U.S. citizenship required); no action.

items.name: Stossel in the Classroom AI Challenge 2026-27
items.note: Hold a conversation with ChatGPT or Gemini on one of four topics, then write a 500-750 word reflection. Prizes are $1,500, $1,000 and $500, plus ten $250 finalist awards. Open to grades 8-12 aged 13+ who live in the US, Canada or at a US military address.
items.act: Pick a topic, save the chatbot conversation link and submit it with the reflection by Jan 18, 2027.

items.name: Wolfram High School Summer Research Program
items.cost: Tuition (amount not listed); need-based scholarships, need-blind admission
items.note: About 80 students each do an original computational research project with a mentor. Students must be under 18 at the end of the program, and international students are accepted. Scholarship requests must go in with the application.
items.act: Apply by Jan 18 for Early Decision and include the scholarship request with the application.

items.name: Paul Kalanithi Writing Contest
items.org: Stanford Medicine & the Muse (Girand Center for Biomedical Ethics)
items.note: Medicine-themed writing contest open to all, with fiction, essay/nonfiction and poetry categories; each winner gets $300 and publication in Stanford's journal Anastomosis. The page sets no age or grade limit, and winners need a U.S. bank account to receive the prize.
items.act: Email the organizers to confirm high schoolers can enter, then submit a nonfiction essay by Jan 18, 2027.

items.name: Notre Dame Leadership Seminars
items.note: A two-week residential seminar (June 19–30 or July 10–21, 2027) on leadership and public questions, for juniors who will be 16 by Aug 1. International students are accepted. Only students from non-English-speaking schools need an English test.
items.act: Next step: check the Fees & Financial Aid page before you apply. Test scores are due by Jan 31.

items.name: C-SPAN StudentCam Documentary Competition
items.note: Make a short documentary on the 2027 theme "Mr. Speaker, I Rise To…": the issue you would raise in your first speech as a new member of Congress. Open to students at U.S. schools, and international students also qualify. Prizes over $600 require a Social Security number and a W-9, so ask C-SPAN how they pay winners without an SSN.
items.act: Pick your issue and line up 2–3 interviews with people on different sides of it.

items.name: Thomas Edison Pitch Contest 2027
items.note: A free national invention pitch contest for students in grades 4 to 12, entering alone or in teams of up to 5 with an adult mentor. Finalists get trophies and gift cards, and the winning schools get makerspace equipment. No citizenship rule is stated.
items.act: Read the 2027 Guidebook on the site to confirm the deadlines, then register after Dec 1 with an adult mentor.

items.name: National WWII Museum Student Writing Contest
items.note: History writing contest for U.S. students in grades 7–12 at public, private or home schools. This year's entry is a poem from an everyday soldier's point of view plus an annotated bibliography of at least five sources. Citizenship is required only for students at schools overseas.
items.act: Write the poem and annotated bibliography and upload them as one PDF on the museum's site by Jan 22, 2027.

items.name: UT Southwestern STARS Summer Research Program
items.note: Summer biomedical research in Dallas for juniors aged 16+ with no prior research experience, aimed at North Texas students. Only U.S. citizens and nationals or people eligible to work in the U.S. may apply, which rules out H-4.
items.act: Not eligible; skip.

items.name: Wharton High School Data Science Competition 2027
items.org: Wharton Sports Analytics and Business Initiative (UPenn)
items.note: A free team data-analytics competition. Data comes out Feb 1, 2027. Phase 1 predictions are due Mar 1, the semifinal slide deck is due Mar 22, and the top 5 teams present live on Apr 14, 2027. It is open to high school students around the world in teams of 3-5, and each team needs a teacher advisor from the students' school.
items.act: Recruit 2-4 teammates and a teacher advisor, and register the team before Jan 26, 2027.

items.name: ExploraVision
items.note: Teams with a teacher coach design a technology that could exist 20 years from now. It's a lighter lift than ISEF.
items.act: Next step: find a teacher coach and two or three teammates, and confirm eligibility on the official site.

items.name: NACLO 2027 (North American Computational Linguistics Open)
items.dlabel: Open Round Jan 28, 2027 (register earlier at reg.naclo.org; confirm)
items.note: Free computational-linguistics olympiad: Open Round Jan 28, 2027, Invitational Mar 18, 2027, and top US scorers make the International Olympiad in Linguistics team. Students who are US/Canadian citizens OR enrolled in a US/Canadian secondary school are eligible, including for the US IOL team.
items.act: Register at reg.naclo.org (open since Oct 12, 2026) and find the nearest university or high-school host site, or ask a teacher to host.

items.name: Summer Science Program
items.dlabel: Late Jan 2027 (confirm; dates announced early Dec)
items.note: Five weeks of team research in astrophysics, biochemistry, bacterial genomics or cell biology. There's no engineering track. SSP counts anyone who isn't a citizen or permanent resident as international, so you'd be on the earlier international deadline, and international applicants submit English-proficiency scores.
items.act: Next step: the application opens Jan 4. Ask SSP whether your U.S. transcript replaces the English test.

items.name: NASA high school programs (SEES, Glenn, GeneLab, OSTEM)
items.note: NASA's high school programs all require U.S. citizenship (SEES, OSTEM) or citizenship or a green card (Glenn High School Engineering Institute, GeneLab for High Schools).
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives, for Glenn and GeneLab only.

items.name: Rotary District 6110 Four-Way Test Speech Contest
items.org: Rotary District 6110 (NW Arkansas, SW Missouri, NE Oklahoma, SE Kansas)
items.dlabel: Club contest by Jan 31, 2027; club entries postmarked Feb 28, 2027
items.cost: Free to student (sponsoring club pays $100); $1,000 district prize
items.note: Students give a 5–7 minute original speech without notes on Rotary's Four-Way Test. A local Rotary club must sponsor each entry. The district champion wins $1,000 and runners-up win $350, with finals in Tulsa on May 1, 2027. It is open to grades 9–12, and the manual states no citizenship rule. Past finalists have come from Bentonville and Rogers.
items.act: Email district chair PDG Ron Petersen (ronsr@cbiradio.com; the manual also prints ronsr@cbciradio.com, or text 417-359-3417) or ask a Bentonville or Rogers Rotary club whether it is holding its contest before Jan 31, 2027.
items.question: I'm a high school junior in Bentonville on an H-4 dependent visa; is there any citizenship requirement for the Four-Way Test Speech Contest, and is a Bentonville or Rogers club holding a contest this year?

items.name: Yale Review of International Studies Essay Prize
items.org: Yale Review of International Studies with Lumiere Education
items.dlabel: Jan 31, 2027, 11:59 pm ET (early bonus by Dec 27, 2026)
items.note: International-affairs essay of 1,000–1,500 words, co-run by a Yale student journal and Lumiere Education. The site says it is not an official Yale program. It is open to any high school student in any country, and most awards are tuition credits for Lumiere programs. Top essays are published in YRIS.
items.act: Register and submit the essay at highschoolessaycomp.org by Dec 27, 2026 for the bonus, or by Jan 31, 2027 at the latest.

items.name: Solar Car Challenge 2027
items.diff: Very hard · requires full team build
items.note: High school teams build solar cars and race them at Texas Motor Speedway on July 18–21, 2027. Official registration and fees are due Mar 1, 2027. The calendar page gives no eligibility or citizenship rules.
items.act: This is only realistic with a school team. Email the event director, Dr. Lehman Marks, at LehmanM743@aol.com about eligibility before filing an Intent to Race.

items.name: USA-North America AI Olympiad (USAAIO) 2027
items.dlabel: Jan 31, 2027 (registration, 11:59 pm ET); Round 1 exam Feb 19, 2027
items.note: National AI olympiad: Round 1 exam (Feb 19, 2027), invitation-only Round 2 (Mar/Apr), June camp that picks Team USA for IOAI/IAIO. Round 1 is open to US/Canadian citizens or permanent residents OR any full-time middle/high school student studying in the US or Canada, and Team USA explicitly includes international students at US schools.
items.act: Register at portal.usaaio.org before Jan 31, 2027 and confirm with your school or an authorized test site for the Feb 19 exam.

items.name: USA Astronomy and Astrophysics Olympiad (USAAAO)
items.note: Anyone can take the First Round exam and qualifying round. Only U.S. citizens or permanent residents can join the U.S. team for the International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics.
items.act: You could take the first-round exam for practice, but the U.S. team requires a green card.

items.name: ERI Economics Competition 2027
items.note: An individual online economics and business case competition with Regionals on Feb 22, 2027 and Nationals on Mar 27, 2027; the prize pool is at least $2,000. Open to high school students living in the U.S., with no citizenship rule.
items.act: Register and pay the $25 fee before Jan 31, 2027 if you want extra case-competition practice.

items.name: Arkansas Governor's School
items.org: State of Arkansas · Arkansas Tech University
items.note: A free four-week residential program for rising seniors. It's open only to Arkansas residents, and juniors get one chance. The program doesn't list a citizenship requirement. If you live in another state, check whether your state runs a governor's school with a similar winter deadline.
items.act: Next step: ask your counselor or GT coordinator to nominate you. You can't apply until you're nominated.

items.name: Stanford AIMI Summer Research Internship
items.org: Stanford Center for AI in Medicine & Imaging
items.cost: $3,000 tuition + $50 fee; need-based aid (apply by Jan 15)
items.note: A two-week, fully virtual Stanford program (Session A June 14–25 or Session B July 12–23, 2027) applying AI to medicine, for students entering grades 9–12 in fall 2027 who have strong programming skills. The official page welcomes U.S. and international students, and need-based aid is open to students living in the U.S. regardless of citizenship.
items.act: Next step: if you need financial aid, submit the aid application by Jan 15, 2027; otherwise apply by Feb 1 and line up one recommender (due Feb 8).

items.name: MITES Summer / Semester
items.note: MIT's free six-week STEM program. Applicants must be citizens or permanent residents with a current green card, and MITES says visas of any type don't substitute.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives before Feb 1.

items.name: Carnegie Mellon SAMS
items.note: Six weeks of math, science and a research project. Open only to citizens and permanent residents, and financial documents are required.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives before Feb 1.

items.name: SeaPerch International Challenge (Wild Card entry)
items.note: Teams build an underwater remotely operated vehicle (ROV). They qualify for the International Challenge through a regional event or a Wild Card application, which opens Dec 1, 2026 and closes Feb 1, 2027. It is open to elementary, middle and high school students, and no citizenship rule is stated.
items.act: Check the regional list at seaperch.org/2026-season for an event near NW Arkansas. If there is none, apply for a Wild Card by Feb 1.

items.name: Carnegie Mellon AI Scholars 2027
items.org: Carnegie Mellon University School of Computer Science
items.note: A fully funded four-week residential AI program for rising seniors, held June 26 to July 24, 2027. Applicants must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents with a current green card, and must show financial need.
items.act: Do not apply unless the green card arrives before Feb 1, 2027.

items.name: Optimist International Essay Contest 2026-27
items.dlabel: Early Feb 2027, set by the local club (confirm)
items.diff: Moderate: essay on an assigned topic, judged first by a local club
items.note: The 2026-27 topic is "Finding My Voice in a World Full of Noise." Club winners advance to the district contest for a $2,500 college scholarship. Entrants must be under 19 on Oct 1 and must not have finished high school, and they enter through the district where they live. The page states no citizenship rule. The nearest club is the Rogers, AR club.
items.act: Email Optimist International to get connected with the Rogers, AR club, then ask that club for its essay deadline and whether it allows non-citizens.
items.question: Could you connect me with the Rogers, AR Optimist Club for the 2026-27 Essay Contest, and can a student on an H-4 dependent visa (not a citizen or green card holder) living in Bentonville receive the district scholarship?

items.name: Quill and Scroll Writing, Visual & Multimedia Contest
items.note: Student journalism contest for work published between Feb 5, 2026 and Feb 4, 2027. The school's adviser submits entries, and there are 54 categories, including editorials and in-depth reporting. The page does not say whether the school must be a member, and it gives no citizenship rule.
items.act: Ask the school newspaper adviser whether the school enters; this only works if you have published pieces in a school publication.

items.name: AIME → USAMO / USAJMO
items.diff: Extreme · only via November AMC score
items.note: Only students who qualified on the November AMC 10/12 take the AIME. The USAMO and USAJMO are open to U.S. citizens and to 'legal residents' of the U.S. or Canada, and choosing the IMO team requires citizenship or a green card.
items.act: Next step: if you qualified for the AIME, ask the MAA whether H-4 status counts as legal residence for the USAMO.
items.question: I'm a high school student at a U.S. public school on an H-4 dependent visa; would I count as a 'legal resident' eligible for the USAMO/USAJMO if I qualify through the AIME?

items.name: Simons Summer Research Program
items.note: Six weeks in a faculty lab. You need a school nomination (up to three per school), and the program is limited to citizens and permanent residents.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives before the school's nomination deadline.

items.name: University of Arkansas High School Programming Contest 2027
items.note: A programming contest for teams of 2 or 3, held in person at UA Fayetteville on Mar 6, 2027. Any high school student in the U.S. can enter, and each school needs a faculty or staff coach. Prizes have included 3D printers and VR headsets.
items.act: Ask a CS or math teacher to coach a team, then register when registration opens on Jan 4, 2027.

items.name: ISTE+ASCD AI Innovator Student Challenge 2027
items.note: Teams pick a local problem tied to a UN Sustainable Development Goal and design an AI-powered solution, guided by an educator. Winning teams are invited to present at ISTELive. It invites students around the world; the earlier cycle allowed grade 9-12 teams of up to 3 with a teacher sponsor.
items.act: Recruit up to 2 teammates and a teacher sponsor, then submit the project through the form on the ISTE+ASCD page by Feb 7, 2027.

items.name: Harvard National Speech and Debate Tournament
items.cost: Entry fees plus travel to Cambridge, MA
items.note: This is a major national-circuit invitational with Public Forum, Congress and speech events. The school must register on Tabroom, and the page states no citizenship rule.
items.act: Ask the coach whether the team can enter Harvard 2027 on Tabroom before Feb 8.

items.name: Texas State Honors Summer Math Camp (HSMC) 2027
items.dlabel: Feb 8, 2027 (full consideration; rolling after; apps open Dec 1)
items.note: Six-week residential camp in San Marcos, TX, with number theory and proof courses plus a research-style component, similar to Ross. Past participants include international students and the page lists no citizenship rule. Initial decisions come Feb 22.
items.act: When applications open Dec 1, start the application and problem set, and ask a math teacher for a recommendation so everything is in by Feb 8.

items.name: Christophers Poster Contest for High School Students (37th)
items.diff: Easy–moderate: one 16x20 poster with the theme "You Can Make a Difference"
items.note: Grades 9–12 students living in the U.S. create a poster showing that one person can improve the world. Prizes are $1,000, $500 and $250, plus up to five $100 honorable mentions. Digital posters are accepted, and AI-made work is not.
items.act: Make a poster with the required statement and submit it as a .jpg through the online form, or mail it, by Feb 11, 2027.

items.name: National History Day (Arkansas, Northwest region)
items.note: Make a paper, documentary, website, exhibit or performance on a historical topic. The Northwest Arkansas regional is at UA Fayetteville, and winners advance to state and then nationals. The rules I found don't mention citizenship.
items.act: Pick a topic that fits the 2027 theme and email the NW regional coordinators (Joshua Youngblood, jcyoungb@uark.edu, or Kimberly Hosey, khosey@springdalear.gov) to confirm eligibility.
items.question: I'm a junior at a Bentonville public high school on an H-4 dependent visa; is there any citizenship requirement to compete at the Northwest Arkansas regional and advance to state and nationals?

items.name: MathQuantum High School Fellowship
items.note: A free online cohort program of about 2 weeks for around 10 high school students, covering the math of quantum information science. The page lists no grade or citizenship rules.
items.act: Apply on mathquantum.umd.edu/apply by Feb 12, 2027 with a statement of interest, a transcript and 1–2 references.

items.name: Clark Scholars Program
items.note: Seven weeks of one-on-one research for 12 students a year. Open only to citizens and permanent residents, and you must be 17 when it starts.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives before Feb 15.

items.name: National High School Fed Challenge
items.org: Federal Reserve (submissions to the New York Fed)
items.note: Teams of 3–8 students in grades 9–12 write an economics research paper on the Fed's annual theme, and selected papers are published in the Journal of Future Economists. No prior economics coursework is needed. The 2026–27 Rule Book bases eligibility on the school: students in grades 9–12 at a high school located in one of the 12 Federal Reserve Districts (or a DoWEA school) are eligible, with no citizenship rule.
items.act: Find 2–7 teammates and a teacher advisor, then register a team by Feb 15, 2027.

items.name: NSDA Student Leadership Council
items.note: This national student council advises the NSDA, writes for Rostrum magazine and creates content. Coaches nominate current members graduating in 2028–2030, and each district may nominate one student. Students outside the U.S. can be nominated, and no citizenship rule is stated.
items.act: Ask your coach to submit the NSDA SLC nomination form before Feb 15, 2027.

items.name: USA Earth Science Olympiad (National Open Exam)
items.note: Any middle or high school student can take the online National Open Exam (registration Jan 1-Feb 15). The top 40 are invited to a June 12-20 training camp in Tulsa, but only students who 'permanently reside in the US' can attend it.
items.act: Email USESO to ask whether an H-4 holder living in the U.S. counts as 'permanently residing' for camp, then register in January.

items.name: University of Iowa Secondary Student Training Program (SSTP)
items.cost: $7,500 program fee + $95 application fee; aid up to 95%, fee waiver by email
items.note: Students in grades 10-11 do mentored research in a University of Iowa lab and earn 3 college credits. International students are explicitly eligible. Financial aid can cover up to 95% of the cost.
items.act: Apply between Dec 15, 2026 and Feb 16, 2027, and email summer@belinblank.org about an application-fee waiver and aid.

items.name: Davidson Fellows Scholarship
items.note: Awards a significant finished project in STEM, literature, philosophy or 'Outside the Box.' Open only to citizens and permanent residents living in the U.S.
items.act: Next year: you're eligible through age 18, so if the green card arrives, aim for the 2028 cycle.

items.name: NYT STEM Interview Contest (video)
items.note: A video of up to 2 minutes built around an interview with an expert on a science, technology, engineering, math or health question. Open to students aged 13–19 worldwide, and AI is banned.
items.act: Find an expert to interview (a teacher, researcher or engineer) and pick one sharp question.

items.name: Stanford Math Tournament (SMT) 2027
items.note: Major collegiate math tournament at Stanford. The in-person event is 'only for US high school students' (international students use SMT Online). Teams of 5–6 apply and are selected; individuals can apply and be placed on a mixed team.
items.act: Form a 5–6 person team with your school's math club, or apply as an individual, when the in-person application opens (around December).

items.name: YIS Global Stock Pitch Competition 2027
items.cost: $30 per person; travel to the NYC Summit is self-paid
items.note: Individuals or pairs submit a stock pitch; registration opens Dec 15, 2026. The top 100 teams are invited to the Global Youth Investment Summit in New York City on May 25-26, 2027. U.S. and international high school students are eligible.
items.act: Register on the MyYIS portal after Dec 15, 2026 and email the pitch before Feb 19, 2027.

items.name: Science fair → Regeneron ISEF
items.org: Society for Science · affiliated regional and state fairs
items.note: You qualify through an affiliated fair, and there's no citizenship requirement. In Arkansas, regional fairs feed the state fair at UCA, and the Northwest Arkansas fair's review committee meets Feb 20, 2027. Becoming an ISEF finalist is one of the strongest STEM credentials. This is realistic only if you already have a project underway.
items.act: Next step: find your affiliated fair. Projects involving human participants need review-committee (SRC/IRB) approval before you start the work.

items.name: Arkansas Personal Finance Challenge 2027
items.dlabel: About Feb 20, 2027 (online Round 1 close, based on 2026 dates; confirm)
items.note: State qualifier for the National Personal Finance Challenge: a teacher registers a team of 3-4, the team takes an online round, and finalists compete at UCA in March; first place advances to nationals in Atlanta with $1,500 in travel support. Eligibility depends on enrollment at an Arkansas school.
items.act: Ask a teacher to register a team in January, and confirm the 2027 dates with Economics Arkansas.

items.name: Stanford SIMR
items.note: Eight weeks of medical research at Stanford (June 7 – July 29, 2027). You must be a U.S. citizen or green-card holder. The program strongly favors Bay Area students, and out-of-area students must live with family nearby.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives and you can stay in the Bay Area.

items.name: Blue Ocean Student Entrepreneur Competition
items.note: Pitch a product or idea in a 3–5 minute video using Blue Ocean Strategy tools. Open to high school students anywhere, individually or in teams of up to 5.
items.act: Complete the free online mini-course first. It's required before you can submit.

items.name: SPJ/JEA High School Essay Contest
items.org: Society of Professional Journalists & Journalism Education Association
items.note: National essay contest on journalism and press-freedom topics, for grades 9–12 at U.S. public, private or home schools. The page says 'international students are not currently accepted' but gives no citizenship rule. The 2027 topic comes out in December 2026, and the application opens mid-December.
items.act: Email JEA to confirm that a non-citizen at a U.S. public school can enter, then write on the 2027 topic when it is released in December.
items.question: I'm a junior at a U.S. public high school on an H-4 dependent visa; does the rule that international students are not accepted apply to me, or can a non-citizen enrolled at a U.S. school enter?

items.name: Stanford SHTEM Summer Internship
items.cost: $95 application fee + $2,500 tuition (aid available); no housing
items.note: A 7-week research internship at Stanford for juniors and seniors. Applicants must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents, with no exceptions.
items.act: Not eligible on H-4; revisit only if the green card arrives before applying.

items.name: Canada/USA Mathcamp
items.cost: Tuition; aid for all, incl. full scholarships
items.note: A five-week residential math program for ages 13–18, admitted mainly through a hard Qualifying Quiz. It explicitly welcomes students from around the world and gives international students financial aid. The 2027 deadline isn't posted yet; 2026's was Feb 23.
items.act: Watch for the 2027 Qualifying Quiz and start working the problems as soon as it's posted.

items.name: NASC National Student Council (officer / state representative)
items.org: National Association of Student Councils (National Principals Association)
items.dlabel: ~Feb 22, 2027 (confirm; 2026 cycle opened Jan 12 and closed Feb 22)
items.cost: Free; includes at least one all-expense-paid trip to Washington, D.C.
items.note: A national student council of high schoolers that runs monthly virtual meetings, campaigns and a funded D.C. trip. High school officer candidates and state representatives must live in the U.S. or a U.S. territory, be rising juniors or seniors, and attend a school with an active NASC membership. No citizenship rule is stated.
items.act: Ask the Bentonville High student council adviser whether the school holds an active NASC membership, then watch for the 2027 application, which opened around mid-January last cycle.

items.name: Arkansas Economics Challenge 2027
items.note: State qualifier for the National Economics Challenge. Teams of 3-4 from grades 9-12, rostered by a teacher, take an online test between Jan 1 and Feb 24, 2027; finalists compete at UCA on Mar 17, 2027 for $500/$300/$150 team prizes and a shot at nationals. Eligibility depends only on enrollment at an Arkansas school.
items.act: Ask an economics or social studies teacher to register a team with Economics Arkansas before January.

items.name: Penn Medicine Summer Program for High School Students
items.org: Perelman School of Medicine (via ESF Pre-College)
items.note: Three-week residential medicine program at Penn's Perelman School of Medicine for rising juniors and seniors, run through ESF Pre-College. The application page does not list tuition, financial aid or whether international students may apply.
items.act: Email ESF Pre-College for the 2027 tuition and aid before deciding whether to apply by Feb 25, 2027.

items.name: PROMYS (Program in Mathematics for Young Scientists)
items.cost: Free under $80k income; up to $8,000; aid
items.note: Six weeks of number theory at Boston University (June 27 – Aug 7, 2027) for ages 14–18. It selects students from the U.S. and around the world and considers aid for international students case by case. The application opens in January.
items.act: Sign up on the PROMYS site to be notified when the 2027 application and problem set open in January.

items.name: USA Economics and Business Olympiad (USAEBO) 2027
items.cost: Fee not stated on the page; check the registration portal
items.note: The U.S. selection contest for the International Economics Olympiad. Round 1 (online multiple choice) is Mar 13, 2027 and Round 2 (free response) is Mar 27, 2027; five students are picked for Team USA. Students of any citizenship can compete, and full-time students studying in the U.S. are eligible for Team USA.
items.act: Register through the USAEBO portal before Feb 27, 2027, then study the syllabus on usaebo.org.

items.name: American Philosophy Olympiad (US selection for IPO)
items.note: A 3-hour proctored philosophy essay, written in French or Spanish, that picks the two U.S. students for the International Philosophy Olympiad. It requires U.S. citizenship or permanent residency.
items.act: Not eligible now; recheck if the green card is granted.

items.name: Apple Swift Student Challenge 2027
items.note: Build an app playground for any Apple platform. Winners get a year of Apple Developer Program membership and a gift, and Distinguished Winners are invited to Apple in Cupertino. Open to students 13+ (in the US) enrolled in an accredited school, with no citizenship rule.
items.act: Register free as an Apple developer and start building the app now so it is ready when submissions open Feb 8, 2027.

items.name: Horatio Alger National Scholarship
items.note: 105 need-based $25,000 scholarships for high school juniors with family income of $100,000 or less. Applicants must be U.S. citizens; the FAQ says permanent residents do not qualify.
items.act: Not possible unless you become a U.S. citizen; a green card alone won't qualify.

items.name: CDC Museum Disease Detective Camp
items.dlabel: Early Mar 2027 (confirm; 2025 apps were due by postmark Mar 7)
items.diff: High (27 seats per week; 702 applicants in 2024)
items.cost: Free; family pays travel and housing in Atlanta
items.note: Free week-long public-health and epidemiology camp at CDC headquarters in Atlanta for students in the summer before junior or senior year, who must be at least 16 on the first day. The FAQ says non-U.S. citizens may apply but must show documents and bring a passport every day.
items.act: Line up a teacher recommendation now and check the CDC camp page in January 2027 for the 2027 application form.

items.name: ASHG DNA Day Essay Contest
items.note: National essay contest on human genetics (up to 750 words) for grades 9-12 in the U.S. or internationally; no citizenship rule. A teacher, counselor or administrator must submit the essay, and each student may enter one.
items.act: Ask a biology teacher in January 2027 to register and submit your essay once the 2027 prompt is posted.

items.name: Science without Borders Challenge 2027
items.org: Khaled bin Sultan Living Oceans Foundation
items.diff: Moderate: 2D science-themed artwork plus two progress photos
items.note: An international student art contest. The 2027 theme is "Navigate With Care" (responsible navigation protecting people and marine life). It is open to students aged 11–19 worldwide and requires a teacher sponsor. The 15–19 age group awards $500, $350 and $200 scholarships. The page also shows a 'closed' notice, so check that the contest is still taking entries.
items.act: Find a teacher sponsor and check the contest rules page to confirm entries are open before starting the artwork.

items.name: √mathroots @ MIT
items.dlabel: Early Mar 2027 (confirm; 2026 was Mar 3); opens early Jan
items.cost: Free tuition, housing, meals; family pays travel (hardship travel aid exists)
items.note: A free 14-day summer program at MIT on creative math and problem solving that especially encourages students who have overcome barriers to learning. Open to students who are U.S. citizens or attend a U.S. high school and will still be in high school in fall 2027, so juniors qualify.
items.act: Watch mathroots.mit.edu/apply for the early-January opening and prepare a personal statement and a math teacher recommendation.

items.name: Arkansas High School Mock Trial Competition
items.org: Arkansas Bar Association · U.S. District Court (E.D. Ark.)
items.note: School teams try a mock case at the federal courthouse in Little Rock; the state champion goes to the National High School Mock Trial Championship (May 13–15, 2027, St. Louis). A training workshop is set for Jan 9. No citizenship rule is stated; registration is by team through Tabroom.
items.act: Ask your debate coach or a social studies teacher whether your school fields a mock trial team and when it registers.
items.question: I'm a junior at a Bentonville public high school on an H-4 dependent visa; is there any citizenship requirement to compete on a team in the Arkansas High School Mock Trial Competition?

items.name: ACTM Arkansas Math Contest (Regional + State) 2027
items.org: Arkansas Council of Teachers of Mathematics / UCA
items.dlabel: Mar 6, 2027 (regional contest; State Apr 24, 2027 at UCA, by invitation)
items.diff: Moderate · top regional scorers go to State
items.note: Arkansas's statewide course-based math contest, with tests in Algebra I, Geometry, Algebra II, Precalculus & Trig, Calculus and Statistics. Regional winners are invited to the State contest at UCA. Fayetteville (University of Arkansas) is the NW Arkansas regional site.
items.act: Ask your math teacher to register you for the Fayetteville regional (site contact: Dr. Shannon Dingman, sdingman@uark.edu) in your current course's test.

items.name: Ross Mathematics Program 2027
items.note: Six-week, highly selective summer program in number theory, built around a hard application problem set. Most first-year students are 15–18, and the FAQ says several international students are admitted each year. The 2027 application isn't posted yet.
items.act: Check rossprogram.org in December for the 2027 application problems, start on them early, and email ross@rossprogram.org if you need financial aid.

items.name: Santa Clara University Summer Engineering Seminar (SES)
items.org: Santa Clara University School of Engineering
items.cost: Free housing, meals and fees; travel scholarships have been offered
items.note: A free week-long residential engineering introduction for sophomores and juniors; international students may apply. Sophomores get priority and it targets students with little prior engineering exposure, so a VEX background makes this a long shot.
items.act: If interested, apply after Dec 1 and before Mar 8, 2027, framing the essay around limited local engineering access.

items.name: Create-A-Greeting-Card Scholarship Contest (20th)
items.diff: Easy: design a greeting card cover
items.note: A company-run contest for students aged 14 and up with a single $10,000 scholarship. Judges post entries for monthly public voting and then pick the winner from the top 10. It is open to legal U.S. residents, and international students on student visas are explicitly eligible. Entering gives the sponsor promotional rights to your name and design.
items.act: Optional: submit an original card design online before Mar 8, 2027.

items.name: Stossel in the Classroom Video Contest
items.note: Students make a short persuasive video on policy topics such as presidential powers or digital privacy. The high school division pays $2,500, $1,000 and five $200 awards. Eligibility is based on location (U.S., Canada, U.S. military address), with no citizenship rule stated.
items.act: Pick a topic and turn an oratory-style argument into a video before Mar 12, 2027.

items.name: Stossel in the Classroom Essay Contest
items.note: Policy essay contest of 500–1,000 words. This year's topics are presidential emergency powers, digital privacy, fraud in government programs, and young people's interest in socialism. The rule is residency in the U.S. or Canada (no citizenship rule is stated), and the high school division covers grades 9–12.
items.act: Pick a topic (digital privacy or presidential powers fit OO/PF prep) and submit at stosselintheclassroom.org by Mar 12, 2027. Don't also enter the Stossel AI Challenge, which would make you ineligible.

items.name: Walton College Fleischer Scholars Program
items.org: University of Arkansas · Walton College of Business
items.note: A free six-day business program on the Fayetteville campus for students who will be seniors in fall 2027, aimed at first-generation college students graduating from an Arkansas high school. The page lists March 14 as the deadline without a year and states no citizenship rule.
items.act: Check whether you count as first-generation; if so, apply between now and March 14.

items.name: Chuck Stone Program for Diversity in Education and Media
items.org: UNC-Chapel Hill Hussman School of Journalism and Media
items.cost: Housing and all meals covered; travel not stated
items.note: A short residential journalism program at UNC for students who will be seniors in 2027–28 and plan a career in journalism. The page doesn't state a citizenship rule.
items.act: Apply on the program's application page by Mar 14, 2027 if journalism is a serious interest.

items.name: MIT Lincoln Laboratory LLRISE 2027
items.note: A free two-week radar-building workshop for students finishing junior year, held July 11–24, 2027. Applicants must be U.S. citizens, and permanent residents do not qualify.
items.act: Not eligible. Skip it.

items.name: World Food Prize Arkansas Youth Institute 2027
items.org: World Food Prize Foundation / Arkansas FFA
items.dlabel: Mar 19, 2027 (paper + registration; registration opens Feb 9; event Mar 31, 2027)
items.note: With a teacher mentor, you write a 5-page research paper on a global food-security issue, then present it on Mar 31 at the U of A Don Tyson Center in Fayetteville. Top students go on to the Global Youth Institute in Des Moines. The page lists no eligibility or citizenship rules.
items.act: Ask Arkansas FFA staff whether non-FFA students and non-citizens can enter, then pick a country and topic with a teacher mentor.
items.question: I'm a junior at a Bentonville public high school on an H-4 dependent visa and not an FFA member; can I submit a paper and attend the Arkansas Youth Institute?

items.name: InvestWrite Spring 2027
items.note: A national investing essay contest (500-1000 words for grades 9-12) for students playing The Stock Market Game through a teacher; the top 10 in each division are recognized nationally. Entrants must reside in the U.S.; there is no citizenship rule.
items.act: Ask a teacher to enroll your class in the Arkansas Stock Market Game spring session so you can enter.

items.name: QuestBridge College Prep Scholars
items.note: Open to any junior at a U.S. high school, whatever their citizenship. It's built for low-income families, typically under about $65,000 a year for a family of four. College Prep Scholars have a big head start in the senior-year National College Match for full scholarships.
items.act: Next step: apply only if your family's income is in that range.

items.name: CMIMC 2027 (Carnegie Mellon Informatics and Mathematics Competition)
items.dlabel: Mar 27, 2027 (contest date; registration deadline not posted, confirm)
items.note: In-person math and informatics tournament run by CMU students, with teams of 4–6 and opt-in merging for individuals. Open to all high school students and younger worldwide; each competitor needs an associated adult.
items.act: Email cmimc.info@gmail.com for the 2027 registration deadline and decide with parents whether a Pittsburgh trip is feasible.

items.name: UNH Future Leaders Institute
items.org: University of New Hampshire, Responsible Governance and Sustainable Citizenship Project
items.dlabel: Late Mar 2027 (confirm; 2026 was Mar 27; opened Jan 15)
items.cost: Full academic scholarship for all accepted students; $200 deposit (hardship waiver by email)
items.note: A residential camp at UNH on governance and ethics; the 2026 theme was 'Governing AI.' Every accepted student gets a full academic scholarship, and the applicant pool includes domestic and international students.
items.act: Check the FLI page in mid-January 2027 for the new application, or email Prof. Nick Smith to confirm 2027 dates.

items.name: Arkansas FBLA State Leadership Conference 2027
items.dlabel: State conference Mar 30-31, 2027; registration deadline not yet posted (confirm)
items.cost: Chapter dues and conference fees (amounts not yet posted)
items.note: The high school state conference is in Little Rock on Mar 30-31, 2027, and top finishers qualify for the FBLA National Leadership Conference. Events include business, economics, public speaking and technology. Students compete through a school FBLA chapter; the 2027 eligibility packet is still 'coming soon'.
items.act: Ask whether Bentonville High has an FBLA chapter and join it so you can pick events before district deadlines.
items.question: I'm a junior at a Bentonville public high school on an H-4 dependent visa; is there any citizenship requirement to compete at the Arkansas FBLA State Leadership Conference and advance to nationals?

items.name: MIT Beaver Works Summer Institute
items.note: A four-week, project-based program (July 5 – Aug 1, 2027) in autonomous racecars, drones, underwater vehicles, radar, cyber operations and quantum software. There's no citizenship requirement, but you must live in and attend school in the U.S. Some courses are online. In-person courses don't include housing.
items.act: Next step: register early and start the free prerequisite course when it opens Feb 1. The summer application arrives in March, and teacher recommendations are due in early April.

items.name: John Locke Institute Essay Competition
items.note: An international essay competition with categories that include politics, economics, law and philosophy. Entry is free, open to students from any country who are under 19 on the submission deadline. The official site still shows only the 2026 cycle (register by Mar 31, submit by May 31), so the 2027 dates are estimates.
items.act: Next step: check johnlockeinstitute.com in early 2027 for the new questions and exact dates, then pick one in politics or economics.

items.name: NYT Open Letters Contest
items.note: Write a persuasive open letter of up to 500 words to a person or organization that can act on an issue you care about. Open to students aged 13–19 worldwide. AI tools are banned at every step, and you need to keep your drafting history.
items.act: Choose the recipient and issue now, and start drafting in Google Docs so the version history is saved.

items.name: Naval Academy Summer Seminar 2027
items.note: A six-day stay at the Naval Academy for current juniors, with engineering and STEM workshops. The page says U.S. citizenship is not required to attend, but an appointment to the Academy later requires citizenship. Sessions run in June 2027.
items.act: Apply on Jan 5, 2027 when the application opens, because seats are filled on a rolling basis. Have your grade summary with class rank ready.

items.name: Mercy Hospital Northwest Arkansas VolunTeen
items.hours: 4 hrs/week, mid-June to late July + 3-hr orientation
items.note: Summer teen volunteer program for ages 15-17 at Mercy Hospital Northwest Arkansas in Rogers and nearby clinics, about 15 minutes from Bentonville. It requires one 4-hour shift a week plus a TB test, blood draw and drug screen. The page does not mention citizenship.
items.act: Submit the online VolunTeen application between Jan 1 and Mar 31, 2027.

items.name: Congressional Art Competition 2027 – Arkansas 3rd District
items.org: Office of Rep. Steve Womack / U.S. House
items.dlabel: Mar 31, 2027, 5 p.m. CT (confirm; based on the 2026 date)
items.note: A nationwide high school art contest run separately in each congressional district. The district winner's work hangs in the U.S. Capitol for a year. Entry is open to Arkansas 3rd District high school students, who must enter in the district where they live. No citizenship rule appears in the 2026 rules.
items.act: Ask your art teacher or Womack's Rogers office (479-464-0446) when the 2027 rules come out, and plan a 2D piece.

items.name: VFW Auxiliary Young American Creative Patriotic Art Contest 2026-27
items.diff: Moderate: original 2D patriotic artwork plus a 250-word artist statement
items.note: Grades 9–12 students submit original 2D patriotic art through a local VFW Auxiliary. National prizes range from $500 to $15,000 for first place. Entrants must be citizens, permanent residents, or have a permanent residence application that is pending and not denied. Whether Krithik qualifies depends on whether his family's green card application has actually been filed in his name.
items.act: Check with your parents whether a green card application (I-485) has been filed for you, then email the VFW Auxiliary to confirm and to find a local sponsoring Auxiliary.
items.question: My family's green card process is underway but I am currently in H-4 status; at what stage (for example, an approved I-140 versus a filed I-485) does a student count as having 'applied for permanent residence' for the Patriotic Art Contest?

items.name: Boys State / Girls State
items.cost: ~$250, usually paid by school or Legion post
items.note: A one-week mock state government where you run for office and pass legislation. Two delegates per state go on to Boys or Girls Nation, which carries much more weight. The eligibility rules I found don't mention citizenship, but some states set their own.
items.act: Next step: ask your counselor or local Legion post how they pick delegates and whether non-citizens are eligible.
items.question: I'm a rising senior at a Bentonville public high school on an H-4 dependent visa (not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident); am I eligible to be a delegate at Arkansas Boys State?

items.name: American Legion Oratorical Contest
items.note: An eight-to-ten-minute speech on the Constitution. National finalists win $20,000–$25,000, and each state winner gets $2,000. Contestants must be U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives before your local post's contest. You can compete through grade 12.

items.name: NSDA Asynchronous Big Questions Scholarship Tournament
items.org: National Speech & Debate Association / John Templeton Foundation
items.dlabel: Apr 5, 2027 video due (confirm; registration opens Feb 1)
items.cost: Free entry (school provides judge); $1,000 top prize
items.note: Each student records affirmative and negative speeches on a Big Questions philosophy resolution. The top 10 win college scholarships of $100 to $1,000, paid once the student is enrolled in college. It is open to grades 6–12, NSDA membership is not required, and the page states no citizenship rule.
items.act: Ask the coach to register you on asyncbq.tabroom.com when it opens Feb 1, 2027, and provide a judge.

items.name: Purple Comet! Math Meet 2027
items.dlabel: Apr 6–15, 2027 (contest window; registration deadline not posted, confirm)
items.note: Online team math contest for middle and high school students, taken during a window in April. A supervisor (teacher or adult) registers and manages the team. The site lists no grade or country rules.
items.act: Ask a math teacher or club sponsor to create a supervisor account on purplecomet.org before April and enter a team.

items.name: Arkansas Forensics & Debate State Championship
items.org: Arkansas Communication & Theatre Arts Association / Arkansas Activities Association
items.note: This is the AAA-sanctioned state title tournament, with twelve speech and debate events. Students qualify by reaching final rounds at sanctioned Arkansas tournaments during the season. It is school-based, and the page states no citizenship rule.
items.act: Ask the coach which sanctioned tournaments remain this season for qualifying in Original Oratory and Public Forum.

items.name: Genes in Space 2027
items.org: miniPCR bio / Boeing / ISS National Lab
items.note: National contest where you propose a DNA/biotech experiment to run in space; the winning experiment flies to the International Space Station, with 25 awards in all. Open to students in grades 7-12 enrolled in a U.S. public, private or home school, alone or in pairs, with an adult sponsor; no citizenship rule is stated.
items.act: Check genesinspace.org on Dec 31, 2026 for the 2027 rules, then line up a science teacher as your adult sponsor.

items.name: MIT Lincoln Laboratory LLCipher 2027
items.note: A free one-week course in cryptography and cybersecurity at MIT Beaver Works, held Aug 2–6, 2027, for students in grades 9 to 12. Applicants must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents.
items.act: Do not apply unless the green card arrives before Apr 12, 2027.

items.name: Create Real Impact Contest 2026-27
items.dlabel: Apr 14, 2027, 5 pm ET (high school team campaign registration by Mar 31, 2027)
items.diff: Easy–moderate: a 30-second PSA or graphic on safe driving
