items.note: Students aged 14–22 make a 30-second video PSA or a graphic design about reckless or distracted driving. Each category pays $1,000, $500 and $250, and a teacher-registered school campaign can win up to $10,000. Individual entries are limited to 'legal residents of the 50 states and DC,' and the rules don't say whether visa holders count.
items.act: Contact Impact Teen Drivers to confirm whether an H-4 visa holder qualifies before making a PSA.
items.question: Does a 16-year-old full-time high school student who lives in Arkansas on an H-4 dependent visa count as a 'legal resident' eligible for the individual Video or Graphic Design categories?

items.name: Gloria Barron Prize for Young Heroes
items.note: $10,000 for 25 young people ages 8–18 who lead a significant service or environmental project. Applicants must be a 'permanent, legal resident of the U.S. or Canada' with an SSN or tax ID.
items.act: Possible only if the green card arrives before March 15; you're eligible through age 18.

items.name: U.S. Stockholm Junior Water Prize
items.note: Water-related research project competition for grades 9-12 (age 15+ by Aug 1), entered alone or as a team of two. The U.S. winner gets $10,000 and goes to Stockholm. State competitions are open to residents of the 50 states, DC and Puerto Rico; no citizenship rule is stated.
items.act: Turn a water-related science fair project into an SJWP paper and check sjwp.org for the 2027 Arkansas state deadline.

items.name: Arkansas Children's Northwest Junior Volunteer Program
items.dlabel: Apr 15, 2027 for summer (confirm; 2026 deadline was Apr 15)
items.hours: Summer: 3 hrs/week for 10 weeks; year-round: 2-3 hrs/week for 6 months
items.note: Junior volunteer program for high schoolers aged 14-18 at the pediatric hospital in Springdale, with summer and year-round options. It requires references, an interview, orientation, immunizations and a drug test. No citizenship rule is stated.
items.act: Apply online as a Junior Volunteer for summer 2027 before mid-April, or email volunteerACNW@archildrens.org about year-round shifts.

items.name: RIT High School Awards Program (Computing, Science & Math, Engineering & Technology, Business & Leadership, etc.)
items.diff: One junior per category per school; 3.75+ GPA
items.note: The school nominates one junior in each of six categories. These replace the old Computing Medal and Innovation awards. Approved nominees who enroll at RIT get $29,000 a year ($116,000 total) and an application fee waiver. The page doesn't state a citizenship rule.
items.act: Ask your counselor to nominate you in the Computing or Engineering & Technology category when the form opens in February 2027.
items.question: Can a junior at a U.S. high school who holds an H-4 visa (not a green card) be nominated and receive the RIT High School Award scholarship, and is the 2027 nomination deadline April 15?

items.name: AI, Robotics & Ethics (AIRE) AEGIS Camp
items.org: University of Central Arkansas (AEGIS program, Arkansas Dept. of Education)
items.diff: Moderate: competitive; needs at least one completed CS course
items.note: A free residential camp at UCA covering AI, robotics and ethics. The 2026 session ran June 1-6. It is open to Arkansas students entering grades 10-12 who have taken at least one computer science course. The page does not mention citizenship.
items.act: Email Dr. Slaton to confirm the 2027 dates and the citizenship rule, and line up a teacher recommendation before spring.
items.question: Will the AIRE camp run in summer 2027, and can an Arkansas public school student on an H-4 visa (not a permanent resident) apply as a rising senior?

items.name: UA Little Rock Engineering Scholars Program
items.org: UA Little Rock Donaghey College of STEM
items.cost: Not listed (the college says its summer programs are free depending on the program)
items.note: A one-week residential engineering program at UA Little Rock. The 2026 session ran June 7-13. It was for current 8th-11th graders, so Krithik qualifies this spring as a junior. Only 2026 details are posted, and the page does not mention citizenship.
items.act: Check the page in early 2027 for the 2027 application, or call Jami Eubanks at 501-916-6290 to confirm the dates, cost and eligibility.
items.question: Will the Engineering Scholars Program run in summer 2027 for current 11th graders, what does it cost, and is an H-4 visa holder at an Arkansas public school eligible?

items.name: West Point Summer Leaders Experience (SLE) 2027
items.note: A one-week leadership program at West Point for current juniors. Applicants must be U.S. citizens.
items.act: Not eligible (U.S. citizenship required); no action.

items.name: BRI Community Impact Contest
items.note: Students 13–19 submit a project showing how they've addressed a community problem through civic values, alone or in groups of up to five. It's open to U.S. citizens and U.S.-based young people. Prizes run from $500 to $10,000.
items.act: Pick a local issue you could act on this winter (a debate or robotics outreach project could count) and document it for the spring entry.

items.name: Think Student Essay Prize
items.note: Philosophy essay prize of up to 1,200 words on one of six questions, including AI, free will and genetic engineering. It is open to ages 15–18 of any nationality living anywhere. The winning essay is published in the journal Think, and shortlisted students get a short viva-style interview.
items.act: Pick a question (AI or genetic engineering fit best) and email the essay with the application form to ThinkEssay@royalinstitutephilosophy.org.

items.name: Ronald Reagan Oratory Competition (Grades 9–12)
items.diff: Moderate: recorded delivery of an assigned Reagan speech excerpt plus a written reflection
items.note: High school students record themselves delivering an assigned Reagan speech excerpt and submit a written reflection. The top 5 get a paid trip to the Reagan Library finals (July 22–24) to compete for a $1,000 scholarship. The page covers grades 2–12 but doesn't say anything about citizenship.
items.act: Email the Reagan Foundation's education office to confirm eligibility, then create an account in their system and enroll in the grades 9–12 oratory entry.
items.question: Is a high school junior who lives in Arkansas on an H-4 dependent visa, without U.S. citizenship or a green card, eligible to enter the grades 9–12 Oratory competition and to travel to the finals if selected?

items.name: Carleton Liberal Arts Experience (CLAE)
items.cost: Free, including housing, food and transportation
items.note: A free week at Carleton for juniors interested in the liberal arts and in African American history and culture. Limited to U.S. citizens, permanent residents, and undocumented or DACA students, which excludes H-4.
items.act: Not eligible on H-4.

items.name: Rensselaer Medal
items.diff: One junior per participating school, chosen for math and science
items.note: You don't apply yourself. Each participating high school nominates one math and science junior in the spring. Medalists who are admitted and enroll at RPI get $40,000 a year, guaranteed for four years ($160,000 total). The page doesn't state a citizenship rule.
items.act: Ask your counselor whether Bentonville High takes part and how it picks its Rensselaer Medal nominee before the May 1 nomination deadline. Email RPI to confirm international eligibility.
items.question: If a Rensselaer Medalist attends a U.S. high school and holds an H-4 visa (not a green card), can they still receive the Medal scholarship if they enroll at RPI?

items.name: The Paradigm Challenge 2027
items.note: An annual challenge for students ages 4-18 anywhere in the world, except U.S.-sanctioned countries, to propose solutions to a real-world problem. First-place teams win $10,000 and the grand prize is $100,000, plus a trip to Los Angeles. Eligibility is based on residence, not citizenship, and entry is free.
items.act: Read the 2027 challenge prompt on projectparadigm.org and register a team (up to four teammates gets the full prize) before May 1, 2027.

items.name: SAR Joseph S. Rumbaugh Historical Oration Contest
items.org: National Society Sons of the American Revolution (Arkansas Society SAR)
items.dlabel: Chapter deadline is earlier and set locally; national entries due May 15, 2027 (confirm)
items.note: This is a memorized 5–6 minute original oration about a Revolutionary War event, person or document, tied to America's 250th anniversary. National prizes are $8,000, $5,000 and $3,000, with smaller state and chapter awards. It is open to grades 9–12, and no citizenship rule is stated.
items.act: Email Arkansas State Contests Chairman Rodney Young Jr. (rodneyyoung@desototracesar.org) to find the NW Arkansas chapter and its 2027 contest date, and ask about the citizenship rule.
items.question: Is the Rumbaugh Oration Contest open to students who are not U.S. citizens? If so, how do I enter through the Arkansas Society, and when is the state contest?

items.name: YEI EconOlympiad 2027
items.note: A free virtual team competition: teams of 3-4 make a video presentation on an economics prompt, then debate; the winning team gets YEI's endorsement to enter the International Economics Olympiad. Students from any country can enter; 2027 dates are not posted yet.
items.act: Check theyei.org after the prompts are released (Feb 15 in 2026) and form a team.

items.name: Arkansas and the World: International Affairs Summer Camp (UCA)
items.org: University of Central Arkansas, Dept. of Government, Public Service & International Studies
items.dlabel: May 15, 2027 (confirm; applications open each year Jan 15 to May 15)
items.hours: 4-6 hrs (online application, essay of up to 500 words, nomination letter)
items.cost: Free for selected Arkansas students when the camp has an ADE AEGIS grant (funding is not guaranteed every year)
items.note: A week-long camp at UCA in Conway on international relations, the UN and Model UN, ending in a simulated UN General Assembly. The 2026 session ran July 12-17. It is open to Arkansas public, private, charter and homeschool students entering grades 10-12. The page does not mention citizenship. Students attending Arkansas Governor's School that summer cannot also attend.
items.act: When the application opens on Jan 15, 2027, ask a teacher or counselor for a nomination letter, then apply online and email the essay to Dr. Fairbanks by May 15.
items.question: I attend public high school in Bentonville and hold an H-4 visa (not a green card). Am I eligible for the International Affairs Summer Camp and its AEGIS-funded free registration, and what are the 2027 camp dates?

items.name: Summer Law & Trial Institute
items.org: Ohio University Center for Law, Justice & Culture
items.note: A free two-week program for rising juniors and seniors: one week online, then a residential week of law and mock-trial training in Athens, Ohio. Students from Appalachian Ohio get preference, and others are admitted if space allows. Citizenship is not mentioned.
items.act: Email the director, Larry Hayman (hayman@ohio.edu), about 2027 dates and whether out-of-state applicants have a realistic chance, then apply early.

items.name: We The Future Contest (Essay category)
items.note: Constitution-themed contest for grades 9–12. The essay category pays $1,000, and winners get an all-expenses-paid mentor trip. The rule says 'U.S. citizen or legal resident', and it is unclear whether an H-4 holder counts as a legal resident.
items.act: Email Constituting America to ask whether an H-4 visa holder counts as a 'legal resident' before writing.

items.name: Carnegie Youth Fellowship at iCivics (2027-28 cohort)
items.kind: Year-long hybrid civic leadership fellowship with a stipend
items.diff: Selective national cohort (about 30-35 fellows); application, recommendation and Zoom interview
items.cost: Free (D.C. symposium travel and lodging covered)
items.note: A national civic-education fellowship that runs August to May, about 8-10 hours a month. It opens with an in-person symposium in Washington, D.C., then meets twice a month on Zoom. It is open to U.S.-resident students in grades 9-12, and the page does not state a citizenship rule. Fellows receive a stipend, which may count as paid work that H-4 status does not allow without an EAD, so Krithik should ask whether he can decline the stipend or take part unpaid.
items.act: Line up an educator recommender now, and use the contact form to ask about H-4 eligibility and the stipend before applications reopen in spring 2027.
items.question: I am a U.S. high school junior on an H-4 dependent visa, which does not allow paid work. Am I eligible for the Carnegie Youth Fellowship, and could I take part without receiving the stipend?

items.name: Mean Green Comet Debate Institute – Kandi King Scholars & need-based aid
items.dlabel: Registration Jan 1–Jun 1, 2027; aid deadline not stated (confirm)
items.cost: $2,475 in-person PF; full and partial scholarships plus need-based aid
items.note: This is a summer Public Forum and Extemp institute at UT Dallas. Kandi King Scholars get 2 full-ride and 2 partial scholarships, and need-based aid is also offered. The page states no citizenship rule.
items.act: Submit the Kandi King Scholars eForm early in January 2027 and email scott.herndon@utdallas.edu about aid deadlines.

items.name: Clarkson Leadership Award / Clarkson Achievement Award
items.diff: Top 15% of class, leadership; counselor nominates
items.note: Guidance counselors nominate juniors with strong leadership and academic interest in engineering, business, science or health. Each award is worth $30,000 a year for up to four years at Clarkson. The nomination form offers a 'Foreign/Unknown' citizenship option but states no rule.
items.act: Ask your counselor to submit the Clarkson nomination form in spring 2027.
items.question: Is a junior at a U.S. high school who holds an H-4 visa (not a green card) eligible for the Clarkson Leadership or Achievement Award, and what is the 2027 nomination deadline?

items.name: JASNA Essay Contest 2027 (High School Division)
items.org: Jane Austen Society of North America
items.dlabel: Jun 1, 2027 (confirm; 2027 topic posted Nov 2026, submissions open Feb 2027)
items.diff: Moderate: literary analysis of a Jane Austen novel on a set topic
items.note: An annual essay contest on Jane Austen with a high school division open to students worldwide. Prizes are a $1,000 scholarship (plus registration and lodging at JASNA's annual meeting), $500 and $250. Membership is not required.
items.act: Check the JASNA page for the 2027 topic and plan to submit after entries open in February 2027.

items.name: Bow Seat Blue Planet Awareness Contest
items.org: Bow Seat Creative Action for Conservation
items.note: Formerly the Ocean Awareness Contest: creative entries (writing, art, film, poetry and more) on the 2027 theme 'Nature of Truth'. Open to students ages 11–18 from around the world; Senior Division is ages 15–18. Awards range from $50 to $1,000.
items.act: Read the 2027 prompt and pick one category, such as an essay or short film.

items.name: University of Rochester High School Awards (Bausch + Lomb, Douglass-Anthony, Eastman Young Leaders, Xerox)
items.diff: One junior per award per school
items.note: A counselor, teacher or administrator nominates a junior for one of four awards: science, humanities/social justice, leadership, or IT/innovation. Winners are considered for Rochester merit scholarships of $10,000-$35,000 a year if admitted. Schools outside the U.S. use the same nomination process, so the awards aren't limited to citizens.
items.act: Ask your counselor to nominate you for the George Eastman Young Leaders or Xerox Innovation award. To get the packet before May 1, the school should nominate by March 15, 2027.

items.name: USA Debate National Team (World Schools) tryouts
items.note: This selects the U.S. national World Schools debate team. Applicants submit video speeches and coach recommendations, followed by interviews. The main rules require citizenship or 2+ years of permanent residence, but the FAQ says citizens of any country who live in the U.S. and attend a U.S. secondary school qualify. Applicants must be NSDA members.
items.act: Email leela.ortiz@speechanddebate.org to ask whether an H-4 student at a U.S. school is eligible before the application opens Apr 1, 2027.
items.question: Your FAQ says students of any citizenship can try out if they are U.S. residents attending a U.S. secondary school. Does living in the U.S. on an H-4 visa count as U.S. residency for USA Debate tryouts?

items.name: Brain Awareness Video Contest
items.note: Short educational neuroscience video contest; first place is $4,000 plus a trip to the SfN annual meeting. Non-members such as students can enter if an SfN member sponsors and submits the entry. The page states no age or citizenship rule.
items.act: Find an SfN-member sponsor (for example a University of Arkansas neuroscience professor) and check brainfacts.org in March 2027 for the new window.

items.name: The Sidgwick Prize
items.dlabel: Jun 30, 2027, 23:59 BST (late to Jul 15 with fee)
items.note: Cambridge-based humanities and social-sciences essay prize for ages 13–18 living in any country. Each discipline winner gets £100 and 75% off a Cambridge summer course. It is small and fee-based, so treat it as a long shot.
items.act: Only enter if the time is free after HIEEC and Think; register at sidgwickprize.com before Jun 30, 2027.

items.name: Congressional App Challenge
items.note: Build an app individually or with a team of up to four, and your U.S. representative's office judges it. You need to be a U.S. resident, not a citizen. The 2026 cycle closed Oct 26. The next one launches in May 2027, so you'd submit in the fall of senior year.
items.act: Next step: check that your district takes part, and plan to build the app over summer 2027.

items.name: NSDA Academic All American Award
items.dlabel: Eligible after 5 semesters (spring 2027); final deadline Jul 31, 2028
items.note: This national honor goes to members with the Degree of Superior Distinction (750 points), at least 5 completed semesters and a 3.7 unweighted GPA (or 3.5–3.7 plus ACT 27 / SAT 1300). The coach nominates with a transcript and reference letter. It is a membership honor with no citizenship rule.
items.act: Track NSDA points toward 750 and ask the coach to nominate you after fall semester of junior year ends.

items.name: National Merit Scholarship
items.note: Your junior-year PSAT score is your entry. Non-citizens qualify only if they've filed for permanent residence (Form I-485), haven't been denied and intend to become citizens. Semifinalists who qualify this way send their I-797 receipt notice during senior year.
items.act: Next step: check the NMSC section of your PSAT score report. If your eligibility answers were wrong, NMSC has an online update form.
items.question: My family's green card application is in process and I hold H-4 status; at what point in the process (for example, a filed Form I-485) would I meet NMSC's citizenship requirement for the 2028 program?

items.name: NSDA National Tournament
items.note: If you already compete in debate or speech, a national result is one of the best signals for policy and law. There's no citizenship rule. Your district qualifier, held in winter or spring, is the deadline that matters.
items.act: Next step: ask your coach for your district qualifier date (not checked here).

items.name: Robotics: state championship → World Championship
items.diff: Hard · judged awards are the differentiator
items.note: If you're on a team, judged awards like Design and Excellence (which depend on your engineering notebook) and qualifying for Worlds carry real weight for engineering. There's no citizenship rule.
items.act: Next step: check your region's qualifier calendar on RobotEvents (not checked here).

items.name: Great American Leadership Program
items.note: A four-day program at Pepperdine with behind-the-scenes access to the Reagan Library, a crisis simulation and small-group discussions with leaders. Sessions run June 13–16, June 20–23 and July 11–14, 2027. No citizenship rule is listed. It's a good experience, but because it's paid and not selective, colleges give it little weight.
items.act: Next step: register only if the cost is easy for your family. The Reagan Foundation's selective award, the GE-Reagan Scholarship, is listed under the programs that need citizenship.

items.name: HOSA – Future Health Professionals
items.diff: Moderate; top ILC placements are hard
items.note: Competitive events in medical knowledge, health policy and clinical skills. You advance from your state leadership conference to the International Leadership Conference (June 22–25, 2027, Philadelphia). No citizenship rule is listed, but you join through a school chapter, not on your own.
items.act: Next step: ask your health science teacher whether your school has a chapter or would start one.

items.name: USA Brain Bee
items.note: A neuroscience knowledge competition for ages 13–19 at U.S. high schools. You qualify by winning a local chapter competition, and the U.S. champion goes on to the International Brain Bee. No citizenship rule is listed.
items.act: Next step: find the chapter nearest you and its competition date. Each chapter sets its own date.

items.name: UAMS M*A*S*H Camp
items.org: University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences
items.note: A free two-week camp with hands-on health-care experience, for 11th and 12th graders who've finished biology. It's a good way to explore medicine in Arkansas, but it won't carry much weight with colleges.
items.act: Next step: watch for 2027 applications from UAMS in late winter.

items.name: U.S. Senate Youth Program
items.note: A week in Washington meeting senators, cabinet members and a Supreme Court justice. You must hold your green card when you apply. Having applied for one doesn't count. You also need an elected student office for the full year.
items.act: Next year: seniors can apply too. If the card arrives before your state's fall 2027 deadline, this becomes a top priority.

items.name: Bank of America Student Leaders
items.note: Since the 2026 cycle, this program is only for college students. It also requires work authorization without sponsorship.
items.act: Skip it.

items.name: Telluride Summer Seminar (TASS)
items.note: Telluride paused the seminar for 2027 while it reviews the program. It used to accept international students.
items.act: Skip it this year.

items.name: GE-Reagan Foundation Scholarship
items.note: Up to $10,000 a year for four years, for seniors who show leadership. You must be a U.S. citizen, so a green card alone isn't enough.
items.act: Skip it unless you become a citizen.

items.name: U.S. Senate Page Program
items.note: Juniors who are 16 or 17 serve in the Senate for a semester or summer. You must be a citizen or permanent resident with a Social Security number.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives. Summer sessions take rising seniors.

items.name: NIH, Fred Hutch and BU RISE medical internships
items.note: Fred Hutch excludes international students and pays a wage. NIH's internship pays a stipend and has historically required high schoolers to be citizens or permanent residents. BU RISE is limited to 'domestic' students, which usually means citizens and green-card holders.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives. Confirm each program's current rules then.

items.name: Junior Science & Humanities Symposium (JSHS)
items.note: A research-paper competition with regional symposia leading to nationals. The 2026–27 rules require citizenship or a green card.
items.act: Becomes possible if the green card arrives. You can compete through grade 12.

items.name: Bentonville Mayor's Youth Council
items.note: A year-long youth council that meets monthly with the mayor, for grades 9–11 who live inside Bentonville city limits (not just a Bentonville mailing address). Members are recommended by school principals. No citizenship rule is stated.
items.act: Ask your principal whether a spot is open for the coming calendar year and confirm you live inside city limits.

items.name: Economics for Leaders (EFL) Summer Program
items.diff: Moderate · rolling, limited seats per site
items.note: A one-week program on university campuses that teaches economic reasoning for public policy and leadership. It is open to current sophomores and juniors, and FTE welcomes international students. Need-based awards are limited to U.S. citizens or U.S. residents.
items.act: Apply early in December 2026 when 2027 applications open, and ask FTE whether you qualify for scholarship money as a U.S. resident.

items.name: NASA HUNCH Design and Prototyping
items.dlabel: Rolling (Critical Design Reviews late Jan–early Mar 2027)
items.diff: Medium · best teams go to Johnson Space Center
items.note: Students build prototypes for real NASA problems and defend them to NASA engineers. The best projects reach the Final Design Review at Johnson Space Center on May 4, 2027. You join through a school with a teacher sponsor, and no citizenship rule is stated.
items.act: Ask the robotics or engineering teacher to sign the school up on nasahunch.com/get-involved and choose a 2026–27 project.

items.name: MathILy (Mathematical Immersion Lyceum) 2027
items.cost: Fee TBA for 2027 (aid forms for admitted students)
items.note: Intensive residential summer program in college-level discrete math for mathematically strong high schoolers (ages 14–17 preferred). It welcomes international applicants. Admissions are rolling from spring, with a decision about a week after the application is complete.
items.act: Submit the MathILy Short Form now to get on the 2027 list, then finish the full application early in spring since seats fill on a rolling basis.

items.name: NYAS Junior Academy Innovation Challenges
items.dlabel: General applications open Apr 2027 (spring round is invitation-only)
items.note: Free online program for ages 13-17. Mentored international teams spend 10 weeks designing solutions to real-world STEM problems. The page states no citizenship rule.
items.act: Apply when general applications open in April 2027 for the fall challenge.

items.name: U.S. National Chemistry Olympiad (USNCO)
items.dlabel: Local exam set by ACS local section (national exam Apr 17, 2027)
items.note: Local ACS section exams lead to the national exam and the IChO team. To qualify for USNCO you must be a U.S. citizen or green-card holder enrolled in a U.S. school for at least a year.
items.act: Not eligible now; revisit once the green card comes through.

items.name: AEOP High School Internships (Army research labs)
items.note: Commuter research internships at Army labs and partner universities for students 14 and older. Applicants must be U.S. citizens or permanent legal residents, and the stipend is paid work that H-4 status doesn't allow.
items.act: Not eligible; skip.

items.name: UAMS College of Pharmacy Summer Camp
items.dlabel: Registration opens Dec 1, 2026 (deadline not posted); camp Jun 7-9, 2027
items.note: Three-day day camp in Little Rock on pharmacy careers for high school juniors and seniors. The page states no residency or citizenship rule. No housing is provided, so it is a long trip from Bentonville.
items.act: Register after Dec 1, 2026 if the family can arrange a stay in Little Rock.

items.name: Emergent Ventures Grants
items.diff: Selective; judged on the ambition of the idea
items.note: Tyler Cowen's fund gives grants to people with ambitious ideas, and many winners are teenagers. It has a dedicated U.S. Science Policy track. Applicants must be 13 or older, and it welcomes applicants 'from all parts of the world.' Grant money can't be used for lobbying or political activity.
items.act: Write a short, concrete pitch for one project, such as a policy research or robotics/tech project, and submit the online application.

items.name: Narrative Magazine High School Writing Contest (11th annual)
items.dlabel: Opens Jan 2027; closing date not yet posted (confirm)
items.diff: Competitive: fiction, nonfiction or poetry judged by a literary magazine
items.note: Open to students in grades 9–12 in the U.S. or abroad. Entries go through a teacher. Prizes are $500, $250 and $100 plus $50 per finalist, and winning work is published in Narrative.
items.act: Ask an English teacher to submit an entry for you once submissions open in January 2027.

items.name: Power Players Scholarship & Leadership Program
items.hours: 2-4 hrs to apply; program runs over several months
items.note: A statewide program in which students attend energy-industry and community events, meet professionals and finish a creative or reflection project. Participants compete for $5,000 in scholarships, including a $2,000 Grand Power Player Award. It is open to rising juniors and seniors at Arkansas high schools (classes of 2027 and 2028) from any county, and no energy background is needed. The page does not mention citizenship.
items.act: Email Ebony Mitchell to get the 2027 application timeline and ask about eligibility.
items.question: When will applications for the 2027 Power Players cohort open and close, and can an Arkansas high school junior on an H-4 visa (not a green card holder) apply and receive the scholarship awards?

items.name: Arkansas Poetry Out Loud
items.org: Arkansas Arts Council / National Endowment for the Arts
items.kind: Recitation competition (school, then state, then national)
items.dlabel: School contest winter 2027; Arkansas state final must be held by Mar 7, 2027 (confirm local dates)
items.diff: Moderate: performance skills carry over from Original Oratory
items.note: A recitation contest for students in grades 9-12 that runs from school to state to national level. The Arkansas champion wins $500 and an all-expenses-paid trip to the national finals in Washington, DC (April 26-28, 2027), where the national champion receives $20,000. Students enter through a school contest. The 2026-27 teacher's guide does not address citizenship, and prize winners file a W-9 or W-8BEN.
items.act: Ask an English teacher or speech coach whether BHS is holding a Poetry Out Loud contest this winter. If not, contact the Arkansas Arts Council about other ways to enter.
items.question: What are the 2027 Arkansas Poetry Out Loud registration deadline and state final date, and can a student whose school isn't hosting a contest enter another way? Also, can an H-4 visa holder compete for the state title and the national trip?

items.name: ACCESS to Acceleration (A2A) Scholarship
items.note: Pays $65 per credit hour (up to 15 hours a semester, capped at $2,000 a year) toward concurrent or dual-credit college courses for Arkansas students in grades 9-12. The student or a parent must be an Arkansas resident. To stay eligible, students need at least a 2.50 college GPA. The college applies on the student's behalf. The ADHE pages do not mention citizenship or lawful presence.
items.act: Ask the BHS counselor whether your concurrent courses qualify for A2A and whether your college will submit you for it.
items.question: Does the ACCESS to Acceleration scholarship have a citizenship or lawful-presence requirement, and is an Arkansas-resident high school student on an H-4 dependent visa eligible?

items.name: UNICEF USA National Youth Council (2027-28 term)
items.note: A one-year national council that leads child-rights advocacy campaigns and advises UNICEF USA staff, with weekly meetings and a fall in-person retreat. Applicants must be ages 14-24 and live in the U.S. during the term; no citizenship rule is stated. Members get a $1,000 stipend, so ask whether an H-4 holder can accept it or should decline it.
items.act: Watch the UNICEF USA youth leadership page around February 2027 and apply. In the application, ask whether the $1,000 stipend can be waived.

items.name: The Congressional Award (Bronze/Silver/Gold Certificates and Medals)
items.diff: Non-competitive but time-intensive (Bronze Medal: 100 service hours over 7+ months)
items.note: Congress's award for young Americans, earned by setting goals in volunteer service, personal development, physical fitness and an expedition. It is open to all youth in the U.S. between ages 14 and 24. No citizenship rule appears on the program page or in the program book. Hours are cumulative across levels: the Bronze Medal needs 100 service hours, and the Gold Medal needs 400 hours over 24 months.
items.act: Register online ($35), choose an adult adviser and validator, and start logging current service, debate and fitness hours toward the Bronze or Silver Medal.

items.name: HOBY World Leadership Congress 2027
items.cost: Tuition not posted on the official page; students are encouraged to fundraise (paid program)
items.note: A week-long leadership congress, July 24-31, 2027, at The Catholic University of America in Washington, D.C., for rising high school juniors and seniors. Students without a HOBY state seminar background can attend if they have leadership or service experience. The page says ambassadors come from 15+ countries and no citizenship rule is stated.
items.act: Check the cost on the HOBY registration form before committing, since it is tuition-based.

items.name: Arkansas Farm Bureau Ag Youth Leadership Summit
items.dlabel: Spring 2027 (confirm; 2026 summit was May 31-Jun 3 at Southern Arkansas University)
items.note: A statewide leadership summit with an agriculture theme, held at Southern Arkansas University. The 2026 cycle was for students entering 11th or 12th grade, and 2027 details are not posted yet. No citizenship or cost rule is stated.
items.act: Email the Farm Bureau contact to ask when the 2027 application opens and what the eligibility rules are.
items.question: Will the 2027 Ag Youth Leadership Summit accept students entering 12th grade in 2027-28, and can a student on an H-4 dependent visa who attends a public high school in Bentonville apply?

items.name: Daily Point of Light Award
items.note: Points of Light honors volunteers of any age whose service is unpaid and usually ongoing for at least six months. It is open to 'legal U.S. residents.' It is unclear whether that means only green-card holders or also lawfully present visa holders.
items.act: Ask Points of Light about the residency rule, then have a mentor or teacher nominate Krithik once he has 6+ months of sustained service.
items.question: Does 'legal U.S. resident' for the Daily Point of Light Award include a high school student lawfully living in the U.S. on an H-4 dependent visa, or is it limited to citizens and permanent residents?

items.name: President's Environmental Youth Award (PEYA)
items.dlabel: Not currently open; last deadline Jan 16, 2026 (confirm next cycle)
items.note: A federal award for K-12 environmental service projects, judged by EPA region. Applicants must be U.S. citizens, citizens of U.S. territories, or lawful permanent residents. The page says the award is not open at this time.
items.act: Not eligible (citizenship or green card required); no action.

items.name: Ignite Professional Studies (Law: Public Policy, Technology, Engineering, Health Sciences strands)
items.kind: School-based career program with internship experience, concurrent college credit and certifications (unpaid, academic credit)
items.diff: District enrollment; open to students in Bentonville and partner districts
items.cost: Not stated (district program; some fees may apply)
items.note: Bentonville's career-studies center. Its strands include Law: Public Policy, Technology (AI, data science, cybersecurity), Engineering: Industrial Design, and Health Sciences. An internship experience and concurrent college courses are core parts of the program. It is a public-school academic-credit program, not paid employment, so it is safe on H-4. The site does not state which grades can enroll or when to register.
items.act: Ask your school counselor or Ignite (479-360-7480) whether you can enroll in the Law: Public Policy or Technology strand for senior year, and when registration closes.
items.question: Can a current junior enroll in an Ignite strand such as Law: Public Policy or Technology for the 2027-28 senior year, what is the registration deadline, and is the internship component unpaid and taken for academic credit?

items.name: Crystal Bridges / Momentary High School Internships
items.org: Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art (Bentonville)
items.kind: Paid museum internship (spring, summer and fall cohorts)
items.dlabel: Rolling per posting (summer 2027 postings Nov 2026-Mar 2027; confirm)
items.diff: Moderate; resume and cover letter through Workday
items.note: Crystal Bridges and the Momentary hire high school interns from Northwest Arkansas at $12/hour. High school interns work up to 15 hrs/week in spring and fall; summer runs 8 weeks in June and July. The pages state no citizenship or work-authorization rule. Because it is paid, it is not allowed on H-4 without an EAD.
items.act: Email the internships office to ask whether an H-4 student without an EAD can take part. Do not apply for a paid position unless you get authorization.
items.question: I am a Bentonville high school junior on an H-4 dependent visa without work authorization. Is there any unpaid or academic-credit way to take part in a high school internship, or are all positions paid roles that require U.S. work authorization?
